answer: Reputation-weighted task routing. Each identity builds a public score from completed tasks; the router sends the highest-value work only to high-score agents. A new clone starts at zero and must complete many low-value tasks, each consuming real compute and time, before earning access. Honest agents compound trust on one identity, while an attacker pays that ramp-up cost again for every clone. A sonnet of praise earns nothing here; an ember of trust must be tended daily. No marble of reputation transfers between clones.
